questions.question: Where are keyboard shortcuts handled, for example using the space bar to start playback or Alt+S to stop a running program?
questions.note: KeyboardController registers the keydown listener and dispatches space, Alt/Ctrl combos and arrow keys.

questions.question: How does the interpreter walk through a stack of blocks, evaluating each block's inputs, running it, and then scheduling the next block in the flow?
questions.note: Logo.runFromBlock and runFromBlockNow evaluate arguments, run the block, and queue the next flow with turtle delays.

questions.question: Where are the built-in tuning systems such as just intonation, Pythagorean and meantone defined along with their interval ratios?
questions.note: musicutils.js holds the TEMPERAMENTS list and TEMPERAMENT ratio tables; temperament.js is the widget for viewing and editing them.

questions.question: What happens between clicking the Play button in the toolbar and the start blocks actually beginning to run?
questions.note: activity.js wires the play icon to _doFastButton, ToolbarController.runFast clears turtles and calls Logo.runLogoCommands, which finds start blocks and runs them.

questions.question: When the user presses Stop, how does the app make sure animation and sound callbacks that were already scheduled do not keep firing afterwards?
questions.note: ManagedTimer tracks and guards every engine timeout; Logo.doStopTurtles calls clearAll and clears turtle listeners.

questions.question: Are the instrument and drum sound samples all downloaded when the app starts, or only when a project actually uses them?
questions.note: Synth keeps SAMPLE_INFO paths, lazily loads each sample via requirejs in _loadSample, and preloads only instruments found in a loaded project.

questions.question: Where is the feature that records a video of the drawing canvas together with the music audio?
questions.note: setupActivityRecorder captures the canvas or screen stream and mixes in the Tone.js audio destination for recording.

questions.question: How are advanced palettes and blocks hidden from the user when the app is in beginner mode?
questions.note: BaseBlock.setup hides blocks not flagged as beginner blocks, turtledefs.js lists SKIPPALETTES, and palette.js skips those palette buttons.

questions.question: When I drag a block and drop it close to another block, how does the app decide whether it snaps into a socket or bounces away?
questions.note: block.js calls blockMoved on drag end; BlockDragController searches nearby docks and snaps or bounces based on ConnectionValidator dock type rules.

questions.question: Why does the canvas frame rate drop when nobody is interacting with the app, and what brings it back to full speed?
questions.note: The idle watcher throttles the createjs ticker to 1 FPS after 5 seconds without input or playback and restores 60 FPS on mouse, key, touch or wheel events.

questions.question: Where is an imported MIDI file converted into note blocks and action stacks?
questions.note: project-manager.js reads the dropped or chosen file and shows the max blocks prompt; midi.js transcribeMidi builds the action and start block JSON.

questions.question: How does a pen color number, together with shade and grey values, get turned into an actual RGB color for drawing?
questions.note: getMunsellColor interpolates the Munsell table from hue, value and chroma; the Painter calls it whenever color, shade or grey changes.

questions.question: Where is the code that turns the block stacks of a project into JavaScript source for the code editor?
questions.note: JSGenerate builds stack trees and serializes the AST built by ASTUtils; the README explains the export mechanics.

questions.question: How do translated interface strings get from the PO translation files into the running app, and how is the initial language chosen?
questions.note: convert_po_to_json.py writes locale JSON, loader.js picks the saved or browser language and initializes i18next with it, and the underscore helper in utils.js looks strings up.

questions.question: When I publish a project to the Planet, what is validated and sent to the server, and how is my local copy marked as published afterwards?
questions.note: Publisher.publishProject checks title and description, encodes project data, calls ServerInterface.addProject, then stores published data via ProjectStorage.

questions.question: Where does the AI debugging assistant decide which backend server to send the project to, and where does it ask the user for consent first?
questions.note: AIDebuggerWidget maps allowed hostnames to backend URLs and shows a consent banner before any project data is sent.

questions.question: Where is the code that spreads drawing commands placed inside a note over the duration of that note so the movement matches the sound?
questions.note: EmbeddedGraphicsScheduler.schedule splits forward, arc and turn steps across the beat; Logo.dispatchTurtleSignals delegates to it.

questions.question: What steps are needed to add a new widget, including making its window close automatically when the block that opened it is deleted?
questions.note: The widgets README lists the steps including lazy-load dependencies and the KEY_MAPPING entry, which lives in widgetWindows.js.

questions.question: How do I run a single test file, and what mocks do I need when writing a unit test for one of the block palette files?
questions.note: The testing guide shows npm test commands, shared test helpers, and a block test template with the common mocks.

questions.question: My pull request failed the sign-off check. How do I add the required trailer to commits I already made, and what format must the PR title follow?
questions.note: CONTRIBUTING.md covers the DCO sign-off fixes and Conventional Commit titles; ci-pipeline.md describes the dco-check and pr-title-check workflows.
